text: The data subject request is a register held as decisions of the local decision-record chain of DP-03, with a record code of a data subject request and no new table, and it is served by four operations on /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests: the open, the decision under If-Match, the read by id and the paged list.
why: No source declares an operation, a schema, a state set, a record code or a person-reference shape for the capability, and a table of its own would be a second lifecycle beside the append-only chain.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.27; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 and 42; ADR-022; the ownership map (no data subject request table)
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, solution architect and the decision-record library owner, before the contract baseline is tagged
impact: If a table is preferred, the register read, the state derivation and the four operations change and the contract gains a storage section; the criteria and the rights do not change

text: The statutory period is a parameter row of rwb-case read through DP-06 at its version in force, its name, value and unit are set by Compliance before the story is Done, and this story computes the due date as calendar days from the received date with no working-day rule; the test fixtures use synthetic periods of 45 and 60 days at versions 2027.1 and 2027.2.
why: NFR-043 states the target as the statutory period, not set as a working service level, with the status Open, DL26, and no source gives a length, a unit or a working-day rule.
read: Program BRD v4 NFR-043; TSD P4 v3 T7; DP-06; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.1
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the rwb-case parameters owner, when DL26 is closed
impact: A change of the period is a parameter row and needs no build; a working-day rule would add one calculation and one test

text: An erasure is executed as one masking_rule row for every role in force with unmasked false from the effective date of the decision, the masking_version of the row set moved on by one and the decision appended in the same transaction; a correction records the field ids corrected and no value, against the policy table created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP and with no policy value changed.
why: No source says what an erasure does to the data, which field ids it covers or who executes it, and the masking table is the only mechanism of this service that can stop a masked field being seen by a role.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204; FSD P4 v3 A2.5; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; the ownership map (masking_rule = P4)
confirm: Solution architect, data steward and the masking-policy owner before the operations are frozen
impact: If the erasure is instead a removal in the owning services, the masking write stays as the immediate effect and an outbound call or an event is added, which changes the operation list and adds a contract

text: The rights are the legacy permission table mapped to the register: Rules and parameters C to open, A to record a decision and the answer, R to read, with the capability area RULES_AND_PARAMETERS kept; no four-eyes rule is added because no source states one for a data subject request, and the access evidence is read from this service's own access-log operation with a case-id filter.
why: The legacy permission table gives C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK and the FSD A2.27.3.3 names roles and no letters, while TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-COMPLY R only in Rules and parameters and RW-SECADM CRUDA in Platform administration.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-016 Permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-008
confirm: Security administrator and compliance and PDPA officer, before the SIT permission matrix is loaded
impact: If a four-eyes rule or another capability area is chosen, the rights of section 10 and the refusal criteria change and one more test is added

text: The legacy rule-version endpoints, the rule_row data row and the SCR-39 reference are read as copied apparatus of the rule-change stories and are left with RWB-P4-E8007-APP and RWB-P4-AD011-APP; the two legacy criteria, the five messages and the four test ids are kept and the rule version of AC1 is read as the version of the parameter row in force.
why: A data subject request loads no rule version and writes no rule_row, and keeping the paths would give this service a second owner of a rule version.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-016 Endpoints and Data; FSD P4 v3 A2.27 against A2.18 and A2.21; the ownership map (rule package registry = P7)
confirm: Business analyst and solution architect, at the story walkthrough
impact: If a rule version is genuinely part of a request, the entry gains a rule_id and a rule_version and one criterion is added; the operations do not change

text: An incident is a record of this service and not a table: two entries of the local decision-record chain of DP-03, each written in the same transaction as its idempotency row, and the incident id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer and to the observability platform.
why: No source names an incident table and the service owns no table of that name; the append-only chain is the only record mechanism of the service (CG-B-P4-07-E8017-101).
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.28; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T-A; DP-03; the ownership map (no incident table); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 42
confirm: Platform administrator and the decision-record library owner, before the baseline tag
impact: If an incident table is required, the entry schema, the read and the operations change and the contract gains a storage section

text: The rights of the incident path are the Platform administration letters of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and not the Rules and parameters letters of the legacy story: C to open, U to hold, fix, close and report, and R to read, with RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-AUDIT R and the case roles a dash; the legacy Rules and parameters C and A belong to the rule-change stories.
why: The legacy permission table of RWB-E8-017 gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK for an administrative journey that touches no rule, while T6.1 places the administration surface in Platform administration.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-E8-017 Permission checks; R-PREC precedence rule
confirm: Security administrator and platform administrator, before the SIT matrix is loaded
impact: If a separate right is chosen for an incident, one row of the SIT matrix and one refusal test change

text: The five steps of the legacy criterion are carried in two entries of the chain: DETECTED and HELD on the open and FIXED, RECORDED and REPORTED on the closure, with the states OPEN and CLOSED and no other state, and the record code and the field shape of a step are fixed by the contract of RWB-P4-E8017-CON.
why: The legacy criterion names the steps and no source gives the record code, the step shape or the state set, and the number of entries has to be fixed before the read can be built.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-017 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.28.2; TSD P4 v3 T4 and T6.3; DP-03
confirm: Internal audit and the decision-record library owner
impact: A third state or a separate entry per step changes the read and the state transitions; the operations do not change

text: A referral is a record of this service and not a table: one record code for a referral, one entry per state change, hash-linked, appended in the transaction that answers the call, with a referral id minted here and opaque to every consumer.
why: No source names a referral table and the append-only chain of DP-03 is the record mechanism of the service (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-101).
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.29; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T-A; DP-03; the ownership map (no referral table)
confirm: Fraud investigator's business owner and the decision-record library owner
impact: If a table is required, the read, the entry schema and the contract change

text: A referral carries four states of its own: SENT on the handoff, RESULT_RECEIVED when the outside answer arrives, FAILED when the outside call cannot be completed, and CLOSED when the case takes the result; the state set is fixed by the contract and no source names it.
why: No source gives the states of a referral and the state set has to be fixed before the read and the criteria can be written (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-101).
read: Legacy RWB-E8-018 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.29.2; TSD P4 v3 T4
confirm: Fraud investigator's business owner, at the story walkthrough
impact: A different state set changes the transitions and one criterion; the operations do not change

text: The fraud flag in force arrives on the P3 answer of the case read as P3 composes it, and the fraud verdict is read from the decision recorded for the case in rwb-decision; this story names no field of recovery_case and reads no table of P3.
why: recovery_case carries no fraud column and no source names the field the flag arrives on (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-102).
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023; ownership map (recovery_case = P3); Architecture v5 slide 41
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) and tech lead of rwb-decision (P7)
impact: If the flag never reaches the P3 answer, the referral reads the verdict from rwb-decision alone and one consumed operation is dropped

text: Aric is reached through one adapter declared as an external dependency, with no owner in the ownership map, one hop, a 2 s client budget and a breaker, and every test uses a fake; the protocol, the credentials and the result channel are confirmed with the integration owner before the build.
why: No service owns the Aric interface and no source gives its protocol, credentials or result channel (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-103).
read: Architecture v5 outside-systems lines; the ownership map; API Specification v4; DP-11
confirm: Solution architect and the integration owner of rwb-integration (P2)
impact: If Aric is reached by a file through rwb-integration, the adapter becomes a consumed P2 operation and the external dependency moves

text: The referral is raised by one explicit call and has no event, no inbox row and no Schedule: the legacy trigger of a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer has no counterpart in the target service.
why: TSD P4 v3 T5.3 declares no event for the module and Architecture v5 slide 14 makes rwb-access a reference-data owner with no inbound event (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-104).
read: TSD P4 v3 T5.3; Architecture v5 slide 14; FSD P4 v3 A2.29.2 step 1
confirm: Solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-decision (P7)
impact: If the verdict handler of rwb-decision raises the referral, one consumed event or one call is added and the trigger criterion is rewritten

text: The staleness refusal MSG-P1-001 is produced by this story because FSD A2.29 VR-P4-029-1 assigns the staleness check to the feature, and the message text is the P1 text carried unchanged.
why: FSD A2.29.3.1 names the stale data product as the validation rule of the feature and TSD P4 v3 T7 gives the message id, while no source says which service evaluates it.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.29.3.1 VR-P4-029-1; TSD P4 v3 T7; Program BRD NFR-014
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-source-data (P1) as the owner of freshness
impact: If freshness is checked by P1 alone, the refusal disappears from this story and one exception path and one message are dropped

text: The referral runs under a service identity and its rights are Platform administration C and U with R for the reads, and the fraud investigator holds R only; the FSD A2.29.3.3 role table names no primary role and the legacy Rules and parameters C and A belong to the rule-change stories.
why: The legacy permission table, the FSD role table and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 give three different answers for the same journey (CG-B-P4-07-E8018-105).
read: Legacy RWB-E8-018 Permission checks; FSD P4 v3 A2.29.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; NFR-051
confirm: Security administrator and platform administrator
impact: If the fraud investigator needs to raise a referral by hand, one letter is added to the matrix and one criterion changes

text: The matrix is one answer over three role classes and a change to it differs from a change to a person's letters in one step only: a change to a NON_HUMAN_ACTOR role waits in PENDING_APPROVAL for a second person and a change to a BANK_USER or PARTNER_USER role is applied in one call by the requester.
why: No source declares a matrix spanning the three role classes, a change to a service identity or an approval step (CG-B-P4-07-E8019-101).
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.30; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; REQ-ACA-010 and NFR-051
confirm: Security administrator and the platform administrator
impact: If every change needs an approver, the state set and one criterion change and the approval operation becomes the only write

text: The states of a matrix change are PENDING_APPROVAL, APPLIED, REFUSED and SUPERSEDED, and the approver of a non-human actor change is a second person who does not hold the requester's identity, taken from the matrix and never from code.
why: No source gives the states of a matrix change or the approval rule of a non-human actor (CG-B-P4-07-E8019-102).
read: TSD P4 v3 T4 and T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS; FSD P4 v3 A2.30; NFR-051
confirm: Security administrator and internal audit
impact: A different state set changes the transitions, the read filter and one criterion

text: The baseline of this story is the role and permission tables created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP on the per-service migration of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; this story adds one index for the matrix read and no table, no column and no constraint.
why: The WP pattern list carries no DP-15 of its own for this story and the matrix tables already have an owner story, so the delivery has to be stated as an index and no DDL.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role and permission; RWB-P4-E1037-APP; DP-01, DP-15
confirm: ACE team as the owner of the schema and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: If a new table is needed for a change request, the migration story and one contract section are added

text: The rights of the matrix are Platform administration R to read and report, U to set and A to approve, carried from TSD P4 v3 T6.1, and the Rules and parameters C and A of the legacy story are read as the rule-change letters of another capability.
why: The legacy permission table and the target matrix place the same journey in different capability areas (CG-B-P4-07-E8019-104), and R-PREC lets the technical specification stand above the story master.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 Permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; R-PREC
confirm: Security administrator, before the SIT matrix is loaded
impact: If the matrix stays in Rules and parameters, the rights of section 10 and the refusal criteria change and the conflict row is closed

text: The mapping of Entra groups to roles is read through the rwb-source-data contract with its freshness stamp, one hop and a 2 s budget, and is faked in every test; this story reads no v_ace_* view and no table of P1, and the missing contract dependency is carried in CG-B-P4-07-E8019-105 rather than added to the metadata.
why: The ACE iam_group rows are P1's under the ownership map and DP-05 forbids reading them here, while no operation exists in a published contract to read them (CG-B-P4-07-E8019-105).
read: Legacy RWB-E8-019 data row v_ace_iam_group; the ownership map; Architecture v5 slide 41; DP-05 and DP-11
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-source-data (P1)
impact: If the read is not published, the matrix answers no group per role and one panel and one criterion are dropped

text: The role class PARTNER_USER is a value of this service's role table, and the partner identity, the partner firm and the partner session stay with rwb-partner (S9); this story holds no partner user and reads no partner table.
why: Two sources claim the partner user and the ownership map gives the partner tables to S9 while the role class of TSD P4 v3 T3.2 stays here.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 partner_user and T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS; the ownership map (partner_user = S9); Architecture v5 slide 41
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-partner (S9) and the security administrator
impact: If partner users are administered here, one table and one operation move into this service and a contract is added

text: An agent appears in the matrix as a role of class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, SY-AGENT with its letters in the T6.1 matrix, and its service identity, its allowed-action list and its run records stay with rwb-agent (P10) and are not read, stored or copied here.
why: REQ-ACA-010 and NFR-051 subject an agent to the same role checks as a person, and the agent runtime is P10's, so the only representation of an agent in this service is a role row.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 SY-AGENT row and T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS; Program BRD REQ-ACA-010 and NFR-051; the ownership map (agent tables = P10)
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent (P10) and the security administrator
impact: If each agent needs its own allowed-action list here, a table and an operation are added and a P10 contract dependency is recorded

text: The P4 register returns a marker and two version labels per field and never a value, a rendering or a clear personal field; its request and answer field names, its marker vocabulary and its read path are fixed by this story and its section 12, and the P1 dictionary remains the only source of a field definition.
why: No source declares the P4 part of the dictionary and the register has to be given a shape before it can be built (CG-B-P4-07-E1064-101).
read: TSD P4 v3 T-A; FSD P4 v3 access by data product; legacy RWB-E1-064 section 12; the ownership map (dictionary tables = P1)
confirm: Data steward and the tech lead of rwb-source-data (P1)
impact: If the register must carry a definition, the read becomes a pass-through of the P1 contract and this story adds no register

text: The approver of a governance load is the role the SIT and production matrices give the Reference data A letter, held as a matrix row and never as a code constant, and the author of a load never approves it.
why: No role holds the A letter in the T6.1 matrix while API-P4-006 requires it (CG-B-P4-07-E1064-102).
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T-A.2 API-P4-006; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 and AC-EXC-P4-004-03
confirm: Security administrator and data steward
impact: If no role is given the A letter, the approval cannot be exercised and the load stays VALIDATED

text: The count of personal fields is read from sys_fields.is_personal at the version in force and reported as a count; no count is written as a constant in a test, a document or a criterion.
why: No source states how many of the 1,366 fields are personal (CG-B-P4-07-E1064-103).
read: Legacy RWB-E1-064 section 7; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; LDM v8
confirm: Data steward
impact: A later change of a personal flag changes the reported count and needs no build

text: An approved governance load is applied by the service's own load path under the same approval, with the load states carried on the load record, and a failed apply leaves the previous version in force and the load in a refused state.
why: No source says which component applies an approved load, when it applies or what a failed apply leaves behind (CG-B-P4-07-E1064-104).
read: TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS; legacy RWB-E1-064 section 12
confirm: Reference data administrator and the solution architect
impact: If the apply is a Schedule, one Schedule and one batch criterion are added and the approval answer carries a pending state

text: Assumption cited in B-P4-07
why: Cited by _work/msr/editlog/B-P4-07.md; see the story body for the default used.
read: _work/msr/editlog/B-P4-07.md
confirm: Tech lead confirms during the verification loop
impact: Story detail may change
